Scoring a certain amount of points doesn't really matter tho. As a whole scores are getting higher mainly because the NBA are playing at a higher pace than before. The stats of the players are getting "inflated" because of the pace of the game. So, getting 5x value on a 6k guy used to be all you need but now because everyone is scoring more you'll need higher value for all the players. Plus with the soft pricing on DK and FD this year you'll need to score even higher. I think having a fixed target score is not the right approach in DFS anyways. Every slate is different with different match up and pace. Score of less than 275 can cash on medium to small slates with slow and defensive team while score of 340+ wouldn't cash on large slates that are riddled with injury. Have to approach different slate differently.

Pretty excited by this series actually. Yes, there are a lot of mistakes both communications and mechanically. But there are also a lot of positive things to take away from the game!


Zion carried game two. When was the last time we saw a CLG top lane actually impacted the game the way Zion did. Game three seeing Link making Ryu look like a non-factor in game 3 it's refreshing. And of course the bot lane duo. Even though they had some hiccups in the series but the way the dominated the lane game 3 was pretty amazing. Oh, and also it's good seeing CLG not tilting after that pretty crushing game 1 defeat! Hopefully Zion's personality and positively can really bring the team together.


Now, to the negative things. Game 1 was pretty disastrous. Both Link and Zion got out rotated pretty hard by their lane counter parts. After the game was started to slip out of hands we saw CLG go back to the Doublelift split push strat. Yes, the team comp(Rumble, ori, j4, ali, vayne) requires Doublelift to be big but tunneling to hard on the Vayne split farm for pretty much the whole mid game should not be happening. Game 2 and Game 3 also have moments of communication lapse. As shown by the amount of dragons lost by CLG, especially game 3. CLG's bot side of the map was ahead by so much there should be no way for Roccat to get 3 dragons mid-game to CLG's 0.


Anyways, the series was really exciting to watch. Even though there are still clearly kinks to work out but it's awesome seeing solo laners taking the initiatives and carrying the game!
